question.problem: An airport manager notes that, on average, $4$ planes each day are delayed by more than one hour. What is the probability that precisely $8$ planes will be delayed by more than one hour tomorrow? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that delays occur independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of airplanes that are delayed by more than one hour on a particular day. Since the average rate is $4$ delayed airplanes per day, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, $X$ can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =4,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(4).$ 

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{4}^{x}{e}^{-4}}{x!}
$$

Therefore, the probability of precisely $8$ airplanes will be delayed on any particular day is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=8) & =f(8) \\  & =\frac{{4}^{8}{e}^{-4}}{8!} \\  & ≈0.030\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
